benchmarks.task_description:
fix(drafts): save sooner and on Ctrl+S so a quick reload keeps the text

Typing and reloading within 500 ms lost the text: the draft is created by its first save, and the flush on pagehide cannot finish an IndexedDB write while the page is going away.

- Autosave delay 500 ms -> 100 ms.
- Ctrl+S (Cmd+S) saves the open draft right away and no longer opens the browser's save-page dialog.

Verified (web build, headless Chromium): typing then reloading after 100 ms keeps the text (before: lost); Ctrl+S then reload keeps it. Not tested: the desktop GUI (no GTK in the sandbox). Biome check passes.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(rbac): bind role to the cluster's custom serviceAccountName

The RoleBinding subject was always the ServiceAccount named after the cluster, ignoring `spec.serviceAccountName`. With a custom ServiceAccount, the instance manager was denied access to the ObjectStore and backups failed:

```log
rpc error: code = Unknown desc = objectstores.barmancloud.cnpg.io "test123-postgresql-objectstore" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:test123:custom-sa" cannot get resource "objectstores" in API group "barmancloud.cnpg.io" in the namespace "test123"
```

The subject now uses `spec.serviceAccountName` when set, and the cluster name otherwise.

Closes: [#11345](https://github.com/cloudnative-pg/cloudnative-pg/issues/11345)

benchmarks.task_description: fix(user): batch affiliations readable under a students context; flag list needs no college Migration 000041 grants the application role SELECT on users.current_student_batch_affiliations with a policy mirroring the students policy (ListStudents failed with permission denied). The permission-flag list route no longer requires a college. Applied with 000040 to the dev database and deployed as aethercode-user:roles2; students list returns 200, flags 200, zero permission-denied errors. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the `ListStudents` route, which failed with "permission denied" because the application role couldn't read `users.current_student_batch_affiliations`, and removes the college requirement from the permission-flag list route. - Migration `000041` grants the application role `SELECT` on `users.current_student_batch_affiliations` through a policy mirroring the students policy, so reads are still scoped to the signed-in student's college. - The flag list route no longer requires a college context by adding `roles` to the optional tenant resources in `authorization.go`. Written for commit 5bb66b1cb05e8169e05a190a154d721a8f214f5c. Summary will update on new commits.

+-- ListStudents filters by batch through users.current_student_batch_affiliations, but the application

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(web): build with the site's real base path so a custom domain works

## What and why

The first deploy (#22) shows a blank page at https://harper.portableinfo.cloud: the repository's Pages settings use that custom domain, so the site is at the root, but the web build was hard-coded to `/harper-pad/`. The scripts, styles and manifest were requested under `/harper-pad/` and returned 404 (the console errors in the screenshot).

- `pages.yml` runs `actions/configure-pages` and builds with `BASE_PATH=<base_path>/`. The base path is empty on a custom domain and `/harper-pad` on `<owner>.github.io`, so no domain is written in the code and changing it needs only a redeploy.
- `mobile-web-app-capable` is added next to the Apple meta tag (Chromium warns that the Apple one alone is deprecated).
- `docs/pages.md` and the comments in `pages.yml` and `vite.config.js` explain the base path.

## Verified

- `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `actionlint` on `pages.yml`: clean.
- `BASE_PATH=/ npm run build:web`: scripts, manifest and icon links are root-relative (`/assets/...`, `/manifest.webmanifest`).
- Playwright (system Chromium) against `vite preview --mode web` at `/`, 12 checks pass: Harper ready, findings, manifest and icons load under the CSP, service worker, IndexedDB save and restore, offline reload, no CSP violations, no other console errors or warnings.

## Not verified

- The deploy itself: `configure-pages` and the base path it reports run only in Actions. Check https://harper.portableinfo.cloud after the merge.
- Safari on an iPhone; Add to Home Screen.
- A user who already loaded the broken page keeps no bad cache (the service worker never registered, since the script 404ed), but a hard reload is the quick check.

## Checklist

- [ ] `make check` clean: not run (needs GTK); no Go changes
- [x] Docs / README updated

benchmarks.task_description:
[Backport v1.32] fix(kubectl): embed release version metadata and expose --version

Backport e208d5a190b8b4c670c0d6aa454fd5c94b709896 from #3717.

___

### What does this PR do?

Embed the release version, full Git commit, and build time in `kubectl-datadog` using GoReleaser's metadata in all four build configurations. Add `kubectl datadog --version` to print those values, with a regression test and usage documentation.

### Motivation

[CONTP-2289](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CONTP-2289): published plugin binaries retain the default version `0.0.0` because the release workflow runs GoReleaser directly, while the linker flags reference variables defined only in the Makefile. The generic configuration also targets an incorrect package path. Users and support need to identify the installed plugin release.

### Additional Notes

The platform-specific release configurations have contained these flags since their introduction in #697. This changes the configuration directly, so the workflow does not need to supply additional environment variables.

The published-artifact acceptance check remains pending until the next release.

### Minimum Agent Versions

No new minimum version requirements.

* Agent: unchanged
* Cluster Agent: unchanged

### Describe your test plan

- Run `go test ./cmd/kubectl-datadog/... ./pkg/version`.
- Run `make lint`.
- Validate all four configurations with `goreleaser check` using GoReleaser 2.4.1.
- Build both macOS architectures with `goreleaser build --snapshot --skip=before --config .goreleaser-for-darwin.yaml`; run the native binary with `--version` and compare its version, commit, and build time against `dist/metadata.json`.
- After the next release, download the published plugin archive, extract it, and check that `kubectl-datadog --version` reports that release's version, commit, and build time.

### Checklist

- [x] PR has at least one valid label: `bug`, `enhancement`, `refactoring`, `documentation`, `tooling`, and/or `dependencies`
- [x] PR has a milestone or the `qa/skip-qa` label
- [x] All commits are signed (see: [signing commits][1])

[1]: https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/signing-commits


[CONTP-2289]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CONTP-2289?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

+// Unless explicitly stated otherwise all files in this repository are licensed
+// under the Apache License Version 2.0.
+// This product includes software developed at Datadog (https://www.datadoghq.com/).
+// Copyright 2016-present Datadog, Inc.
+
+package datadog
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"k8s.io/cli-runtime/pkg/genericclioptions"
+
+	"github.com/DataDog/datadog-operator/pkg/version"
+)
+
+func TestVersionFlag(t *testing.T) {
+	originalVersion, originalCommit, originalBuildTime := version.Version, version.Commit, version.BuildTime
+	t.Cleanup(func() {
+		version.Version, version.Commit, version.BuildTime = originalVersion, originalCommit, originalBuildTime
+	})
+	version.Version = "1.32.0-rc.1"
+	version.Commit = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567"
+	version.BuildTime = "2026-11-03T08:00:00Z"
+
+	streams, _, out, errOut := genericclioptions.NewTestIOStreams()
+	cmd := NewCmd(streams)
+	cmd.SetArgs([]string{"--version"})
+
+	require.NoError(t, cmd.Execute())
+	require.Equal(t, "Version: 1.32.0-rc.1\nGit Commit: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567\nBuild time: 2026-11-03T08:00:00Z\n", out.String())
+	require.Empty(t, errOut.String())
+}
